Industry observers note that although individual variation in protein amino acid sequences can exist between individuals, we find, among the regions of the proteins covered in our ancient data, only a single position with sequence variation among the worldwide distributed modern humans included in our database search (Table 1). In general, among extant hominids, out of the 43 amino acid positions variable among and between great ape individuals included, and in cases in which we have coverage for at least one of the four hominins studied here, only five positions contain sequence heterogeneity between the included individuals where at least four or more individuals of a single genus share variation (one position in H. sapiens, three in the genus Pan and one in the genus Pongo; Table 1). Notably, the four teeth carrying the derived AMBN A253G substitution shared with the previously reported H. erectus specimens from Zhoukoudian, Sunjiadon and Hexian differ from those six specimens, as the Naxian and Baxian hominins do not carry the derived AMBN M273V substitution (Table 1, Fig. 4 and Extended Data Fig. 3). Thus, the observation of the AMBN Gly253 substitution combined with the observation at AMBN Met273 in four hominin teeth, of at least three individuals, if the two M1s from Naxian cave represent the same individual, from two late Middle Pleistocene sites suggests that the hominin population to which they collectively belonged has not previously been sampled using molecular methods, either genetic or proteomic.

Industry observers note that to further explore the phylogenetic placement of the Naxian and Baxian specimens, we conducted a Bayesian phylogenetic analysis. Note that, owing to the sparseness of dental enamel proteomic data, such analyses in palaeoproteomics generally have to assume that there has been no recent gene flow between the individuals and populations included in the analysis. We find that the four Naxian and Baxian individuals with the AMBN A253G substitution cluster together in a clade outside the branch of previously reported Denisovans, Neanderthals and modern humans (Fig. 4 and Extended Data Figs. 4 and 5). The topology of the clade formed by Denisovans, Neanderthals and modern humans matches the expected configuration in the main analysis, albeit with low internal node support (Fig. 4). The topology of these three hominin populations changes once additional modern human and great ape individuals are added to the phylogenetic analysis (Extended Data Figs. 4 and 5). The expected topology of this clade is challenging to obtain when using proteomic data from dental enamel proteins, as reported previously29,39,40, and it is evidenced by the low support value of this clade in our analyses (Fig. 4 and Extended Data Figs. 4–6). Nevertheless, the values supporting the nodes for the remaining branches, including the one placing the Naxian and Baxian specimens as an outgroup to the other hominins, are high in all analyses (>0.995). The Naxian and Baxian individuals are placed in a clade together with six previously reported H. erectus specimens. Those six specimens are placed together with strong support and separate from the four Naxian and Baxian individuals carrying the AMBN A253G substitution (Fig. 4). This strengthens the notion that these four Naxian and Baxian cave specimens represent a H. erectus hominin population that has not been sampled molecularly before. Furthermore, the phylogenetic analysis suggests that, although based on sparse data, this hominin population might have diverged before the divergence of the common ancestor of modern humans, Neanderthals and Denisovans. These phylogenetic observations are in accordance with the morphological analysis of these specimens, strengthening the case that these specimens belong to a previously unsampled lineage of H. erectus.

It has been revealed that by contrast, proteomic analysis of PA1796 from Baxian cave reveals that this specimen does not contain the derived AMBN A253G amino acid substitution (Extended Data Fig. 6b). It has no uniquely derived substitutions compared to the other four teeth, nor does it share uniquely derived amino acid substitutions with the Denisovan, Neanderthal or modern human individuals present in our reference panel (Table 1). Phylogenetic analysis of this specimen places it outside of the H. erectus clade, with varying topologies with low support in relation to its placement in relation to archaic hominins (Denisovans and Neanderthals) or the clade including Neanderthals, Denisovans and modern humans (Fig. 4 and Extended Data Fig. 6a). The protein sequences reconstructed for this tooth are therefore different from the other four specimens studied proteomically, mirroring the morphological analysis that also indicates this specimen represents a taxon other than H. erectus. Only a single Denisovan genomic reference is right now available, the D3 specimen from Denisova cave, Russia, implying that our understanding of protein sequence polymorphisms for Denisovans is by definition limited. Future morphological and genomic or proteomic research on hominin teeth from the region could provide additional frameworks to allow more precise taxonomic classification of PA1796 into a non-erectus group, representing either southern Asian representatives of Denisovans (H. longi) or potentially another population or species.

Eight of the late Middle Pleistocene Homo teeth from the Naxian and Baxian caves exhibit metric and morphological features that lie within the range of East and Southeast Asian H. erectus and that differ from those of Denisovans (H. longi), Neanderthals (H. neanderthalensis), or Pleistocene and Holocene modern humans (H. sapiens). The palaeoproteomic evidence provides further confirmation that four of these teeth indeed fall outside of the known genetic and proteomic sequence variation of H. neanderthalensis, H. longi and H. sapiens, but are consistent with a H. erectus-derived substitution recently described for Chinese specimens dating to around 0.4 Ma (ref. 13). The recovered proteomic evidence is therefore compatible with the morphological data. Dated to between 324 and 184 ka (ref. 12), these H. erectus teeth substantially extend the known temporal range of H. erectus fossils on the Asian mainland, bringing the extent of the mainland H. erectus fossil record closer to the latest known Javanese H. erectus, dated to 117–108 ka (ref. 8). The recovery of a unique proteomic signature of mainland H. erectus from the Middle Pleistocene of East Asia furthermore suggests that specimens attributed to this species could harbour several hominin populations13, and make it possible to molecularly test whether other H. erectus fossils from the region that could potentially date to the late Middle Pleistocene, such as those from Changyang cave (Hubei province, China)11,22 and Chaoxian cave (Anhui Province, China)23, also represent specimens belonging to the same mainland H. erectus hominin population, or whether they have a proteomic signature more similar to earlier H. erectus13.

Recent findings suggest that the discovery of the Naxian and Baxian H. erectus specimens in the late Middle Pleistocene of southern East Asia enriches the hominin occupation scenario in the region. A Denisovan mandible has been described from the Penghu channel off the coast of Taiwan, dating to either 190–130 or 70–10 ka (refs. 7,48). In Laos, based on morphological analysis, a Denisovan molar has been described from Tam Ngu Hao 2, dating to between 163 and 131 ka (ref. 6). Genetic evidence on the timing of Denisovan introgression into the genomes of living humans also suggests that Denisovans were present in East and/or Southeast Asia well into the Late Pleistocene1,49. Moreover, several craniodental remains, such as Harbin, Penghu 1 and Xiahe 1, were identified molecularly as H. longi (Denisovans)7,9,17,19, and several other late Middle Pleistocene specimens probably belong to this population as well (for example, Xujiayao and Hualongdong), including also some non-erectus fossils from southern Asia (for example, Maba, Narmada, TNH2-1)6,50. It therefore seems plausible that the H. erectus population represented by the fossils from Naxian and Baxian cave on the mainland existed in relatively close proximity to Denisovan hominins.

It has been revealed that even though the geometric morphometric analysis of the EDJ suggest that the PA1796 M2 retains plesiomorphic aspects (mostly due to the short EDJ height), the specimen also differs from the morphology of the comparative H. erectus sample (Supplementary Note 2). The lack of a comparative sample for Denisovans (H. longi) represents a substantial bias in our ability to morphologically identify them. The non-metric morphology of PA1796 differs markedly from that of Chinese H. erectus by the lack of wrinkling on the EDJ, the absence of accessory fossae, the relatively large talon and the lingually shifted hypocone25,26 (Supplementary Notes 1 and 2). Moreover, the palaeoproteomic analysis of PA1796 highlights a different signal compared to the other Baxian and Naxian specimens, as well as to the six H. erectus teeth from Zhoukoudian, Hexian and Sunjiadong13 (Fig. 4), strongly suggesting the presence of a hominin population other than H. erectus in Baxian cave. However, among the protein sequences available to us now, the PA1796 specimen does not exhibit the known proteomic variation associated with Denisovans, although it should be acknowledged that only a single Denisovan reference genome is right now available. PA1796 could therefore either represent a still-unrecognized H. erectus group that would differ in molecular and morphological aspects from the currently known H. erectus specimens, a hypothesis that we consider unlikely (Supplementary Note 2) but cannot outright reject, or belong to a non-erectus group, possibly related to H. longi. Future morphological and proteomic research on hominin teeth from the region, as well as the availability of a growing number of Denisovan genomes and proteomes, could therefore provide additional frameworks to allow a more precise classification of the PA1796 specimen.

Industry observers note that the H. erectus specimens from Baxian and Naxian caves extend the geographical and temporal extent of mainland Asian H. erectus well into the late Middle Pleistocene. Occupying rainforest environments12, these H. erectus populations probably co-existed in close spatial and temporal proximity to southern Asian Denisovans. Mainland Southeast Asia therefore appears as a key region to study the evolution, genetics and archaeologically visible behaviours of multiple sympatric hominin species.

The Baxian and Naxian hominin specimens were scanned using X-ray microtomography using the 225 kV micro-computed tomography scanner at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology (IVPP, Beijing, China) according to the following parameters: 140 kV voltage, 120 µA, 0.5 angular increment one step and 360° of rotation. The final volumes were reconstructed with isotropic voxel sizes of 15.7–32.0 µm. A semi-automatic threshold-based segmentation was carried out in Avizo v.7.1 (FEI Visualization Sciences Group) and a volumetric reconstruction was then generated for each specimen. A full morphological description of each tooth can be found in Supplementary Note 1.

In a recent development, dental surface models were imported in Geomagic Design v. X 64 (3D Systems, Rock Hill) to separate the crown from the tooth roots. The crown and roots were digitally isolated at the cervix using the cervix-best-fit plane as a reference51. Five variables were then measured or calculated: (1) Ve, the volume of the enamel cap (mm3); (2) SEDJ, the surface area of the EDJ (mm2); (3) Vcdp, the volume of the crown dentine and pulp (mm3); (4) 3DAET, 3D average enamel thickness (Ve/SEDJ; mm)52; (5) 3DRED, the ratio of 3D average enamel thickness to 3D average dentine thickness (Ve1/3/Vcdp1/3 × 10)53.

In a recent development, diffeomorphic surface matching was applied to analyse the EDJ shape of the least worn teeth from Baxian and Naxian caves (methodological details are provided in Supplementary Note 2). This landmark-free, mesh-based approach was previously demonstrated to efficiently distinguish the EDJ of various hominin species6,22,27. Owing to occlusal wear, the apex of the dentine horns of some of the specimens had to be reconstructed before the analysis (Supplementary Note 2 and Supplementary Figs. 18 and 21). We first confirmed that the EDJ of the Baxian and Naxian specimens differed from that of Pongo and belonged to Homo (which was also confirmed independently by palaeoproteomics). We then compared the Baxian and Naxian EDJs to those of H. erectus s.l., H. neanderthalensis, H. longi and H. sapiens. The H. erectus sample includes dental remains from African and Asia that are regarded by some as belonging to H. ergaster and H. erectus s.s. (Supplementary Table 3). We indicated the labels of the H. erectus specimens in Fig. 2 to show the distribution of the African and Asian material in the morphospace. Canonical variate analyses were conducted and the Baxian and Naxian specimens, as well as the Denisovan molar from Tam Ngu Hao 2 (ref. 6), were projected a posteriori into the canonical variate analysis morphospace. Typicality probabilities were computed for the Naxian and Baxian teeth to provide a quantitative estimation of their most likely taxonomic attribution.

In a recent development, for Naxian cave, fauna and hominin specimens were sampled using a handheld drill with a diamond-tipped drill bit, resulting in between 10 mg and 97 mg of powder for the faunal samples and up to 6 mg of hominin dental enamel. For Baxian cave, dentine was obtained using a handheld drill (36.5 and 43.2 mg of powder), while the dental enamel was sampled using an acid etch. All sampling and extraction steps were conducted in ancient molecular laboratories regularly used for ancient DNA and/or ancient protein analysis, including standard procedures to prevent contamination from occurring in the sampling and extraction environments, including wearing full body suits, hairnets, multiple layers of nitrile gloves, footies and positive air pressure.

Recent findings suggest that dental enamel extracts for Naxian cave were generated using 5% HCl, following previously published protocols31,54. Likewise, dental enamel extracts from the acid etching of the Baxian cave specimens followed previously published protocols54. The dentine samples of fauna from Naxian cave were extracted using a variant on previously published EDTA-based protocols55. For Baxian cave, the hominin dentine extractions followed a HCl-based protocol commonly used for ZooMS analysis, but with modifications to separate protein fragments by size9,56. Full protein extraction protocols are provided in Supplementary Note 3.

Faunal extracts from Naxian cave were separated on the EASY-nLC 1200 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) system coupled to a Exploris 480 Orbitrap mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Hominin dental enamel extracts from Naxian cave were analysed on the Vanquish Neo UPLC (Thermo Fisher Scientific) system coupled to a Exploris 480 Orbitrap mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Dentine extracts from Baxian cave were first analysed on the Bruker Autoflex MaX MALDI-ToF MS instrument. Subsequent to the detection of collagen peptides, both the dentine and the dental enamel extracts from Baxian cave were analysed on an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled to an Easy n-LC 1200 HPLC system (Thermo Fisher Scientific) over a 120 min gradient. Blank extractions were included in all cases to monitor the existence of exogenous contaminants during the procedure.

Industry observers note that raw data files were searched separately by tissue type and cave site, using PEAKS, pFind and MaxQuant in parallel. Initial searches in PEAKS revealed the possibility of a unique substitution in AMBN, while PEAKS and pFind informed on the composition of post-translational modifications (PTMs) that should be taken into account. After initial searches, final searches using an updated protein sequence database and updated PTM information for dental enamel and the full human proteome for dentine were performed (further details are provided in Supplementary Note 3).

Protein deamidation was calculated according to a previous study for MaxQuant data57. Other PTM ratio analyses were conducted by peptide-spectrum match spectral counts or peptide counts, unless indicated differently (applying to MaxQuant, pFind and/or PEAKS). Unipept analysis was carried out using all peptide matches against endogenous, dental-enamel-specific proteins58. As described above, a project-specific database was used for data analysis that includes protein sequence variation beyond that available within UniProt. As a result, Unipept analysis will not be able to match all peptides to the same taxonomic level as the one present in the protein sequence database used. Sequence reconstruction was performed for pFind, PEAKS and MaxQuant data jointly, resulting in a single protein sequence reconstruction for each specimen. Specifically, sequences from different search engines were overlaid for each specimen to generate a single protein consensus sequence. Amino acid positions where PEAKS, pFind and MaxQuant disagreed with each other were not called, and reversed to ‘X’. Positions possibly phylogenetically informative were manually inspected, fragment ion series were checked and E values were assessed. Where necessary, positions potentially introducing invalid sequences were subsequently removed from the protein sequence reconstructions. The consensus sequences were subsequently aligned to a subset of the PaleoProPhyler database of hominid dental enamel sequences, which included four individuals from each of the genera Pongo, Gorilla and Pan, as well as three Neanderthals41,42,43, one Denisovan44 and three present-day H. sapiens from the sub-Saharan Yoruba population. We also added the dental enamel protein sequences for Homo antecessor29 and Penghu 1 (ref. 7) (a Denisovan individual) and carried out Bayesian phylogenetic analysis of the Naxian–Baxian individuals using a combination of different proteins for each tree. The combinations are indicated in each figure (Extended Data Figs. 4–6 and Supplementary Figs. 33–43). The available H. erectus protein sequences from a single specimen (D4163) from Dmanisi, Georgia, were not included in the phylogenetic analysis carried out here because the phylogenetic position of the specimen could not be resolved in the original study29.

#49331. Mikel Arteta shuts down Arsenal team news loophole exposed by Christos Tzolis

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (859 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Mikel Arteta shuts down Arsenal team news loophole exposed by Christos Tzolis

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (859 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 18:48.
  • Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has confirmed that fresh measures have been introduced to prevent players from accidentally revealing confidential team news through Fantasy Premier League (FPL).
  • The decision follows an incident involving Christos Tzolis, whose selections in the popular fantasy football game offered an unexpected insight into his availability ahead of Arsenal's Premier League victory over Liverpool earlier this month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 18:48.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has confirmed that fresh measures have been introduced to prevent players from accidentally revealing confidential team news through Fantasy Premier League (FPL).

The decision follows an incident involving Christos Tzolis, whose selections in the popular fantasy football game offered an unexpected insight into his availability ahead of Arsenal's Premier League victory over Liverpool earlier this month.

According to The Athletic, Arsenal players have been banned from selecting themselves or their teammates in their FPL squads, reducing the risk of injuries and potential starting line-ups being disclosed before official announcements.

Arteta confirmed the intervention during Friday's press conference ahead of Saturday's trip to Newcastle United, stressing that protecting information about his squad was essential to maintaining trust within the club.

The development is particularly interesting given that Sports Mole was among the outlets to highlight Tzolis's revealing Fantasy Premier League decisions before Arsenal's visit to Anfield on November 1.

Tzolis had been sidelined for approximately a month with a hamstring injury, missing six consecutive Arsenal matches before the trip to Liverpool.

Although Arteta had confirmed that the Greek international had returned to training, his involvement at Anfield remained uncertain.

However, the winger provided a significant indication of his fitness through his own Fantasy Premier League account.

Tzolis transferred himself into his team and selected himself as captain, effectively doubling the points he would earn if he made a successful return.

The decision attracted attention because fantasy managers generally avoid selecting injured players, particularly when using the captaincy on an individual who might not feature.

Sports Mole had already identified the potential significance of those choices in its November 1 report on Tzolis's Fantasy Premier League injury clues.

The same report noted that the former Norwich City winger had retained Riccardo Calafiori in his fantasy squad despite the defender also facing questions over his fitness.

Both players subsequently started at Anfield, where Arsenal secured a 1-0 victory.

Tzolis's activity attracted further attention in the following gameweek.

Ahead of Arsenal's home meeting with Hull City on November 7, the 24-year-old reportedly activated his wildcard, allowing him to make unlimited transfers, and removed every Arsenal player from his fantasy team.

Among those transferred out were Tzolis himself, Calafiori and Ezri Konsa.

Those decisions did not establish who would or would not start against Hull, but they demonstrated how closely players' fantasy activity could be monitored for potential clues.

Tzolis has also previously spoken openly about his enthusiasm for the game.

After Arsenal's opening-day victory over Coventry City, he discussed the points he had accumulated through his own performance, revealing that he had selected himself as captain.

What initially appeared to be a harmless aspect of the player's enjoyment of football has now prompted a response from his manager.

Asked whether he had addressed the issue with his players, Arteta confirmed that discussions had taken place involving Tzolis and other members of the squad.

"With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well," the Arsenal manager remarked.

Recent findings suggest that "They're constantly asking me about this as well, because they want to know. It's a topic.".

Arteta acknowledged that the popularity of Fantasy Premier League had created a relatively upcoming challenge for clubs seeking to protect information about their players.

"These are the kind of things that are happening in our society right now," he explained.

Recent findings suggest that "It's something latest. We haven't dealt with it before and we need to put new things in place.".

The Spaniard then emphasised the importance of maintaining confidentiality within the dressing room and coaching staff.

"The confidentiality is something critical because it's about trust and what you're trying to do, and that should be kept as a huge secret.".

Arteta added that measures would be taken to prevent further incidents and subsequently confirmed that restrictions were already in place.

The reported policy does not prevent Arsenal players from participating in Fantasy Premier League altogether.

Instead, it specifically targets the selection of Arsenal footballers in their own fantasy teams, limiting the possibility that transfers or captaincy choices reveal information unavailable to opponents and supporters.

Arsenal are not the first Premier League club to confront the problem.

Chelsea faced similar concerns in October after fantasy accounts associated with players and staff appeared to offer clues about Joao Pedro's injury before his absence against Tottenham Hotspur became public.

The Brazilian had reportedly been removed from several fantasy teams ahead of that fixture, prompting speculation about his availability.

Chelsea subsequently warned staff about the risks of revealing confidential information through the game.

For Arsenal, the issue is especially relevant as Arteta attempts to maintain his side's position at the top of the Premier League.

The Gunners travel to Newcastle on Saturday with a five-point advantage over their nearest challengers, and the manager will be keen to avoid giving opponents unnecessary information about his selection decisions.

Tzolis's fantasy activity may have provided an early indication of his return against Liverpool, but Arsenal's new restrictions are designed to ensure that future team news emerges through official channels rather than virtual football transfers.

Industry observers note that with just a few days until the return of AC Milan action, the international break is now done. Let’s take a look at how the internationals fared.

It has been revealed that whether you love it or you hate it, the international break is now over and players are trickling back into Milanello. Even those who didn’t head away are only just really returning, with Ruben Amorim offering the squad a week off.

Recent findings suggest that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

So, let’s look at what Amorim has returning, with several things to shout about….

Sources indicate that christian Pulisic probably leaves the break as the star of the week(s). His brace against Haiti helped secure a place in the CONCACAF Nations League semifinals, and he then rounded it off with a bicycle kick in the second leg.

After missing the penultimate international break of the season – to ensure he was fully back to fitness – he’s swiftly reminded everyone of how vital he can be for club and country, scoring his seventh goal of the season in only 13 games.

He’s on fire and there are no signs of him slowing down anytime soon.

You’d then have to speak about Diego Moreira, who has left the international break – somehow – with more praise than he started it with. He starred in Belgium’s 2-1 win against Turkiye and then followed that up with a goal against Italy.

Sources indicate that it gets to a point where you run out of superlatives to describe a player and his teammates are already at that stage. Both Mark Van Bommel and Koni De Winter have called him crazy (in a good way), with the former even putting him in the same group as Kevin De Bruyne and Jeremy Doku.

He’s become a starter for the Red Devils and it’s difficult to see that changing.

In a recent development, in terms of the Italians, Milan had a few reasons to smile and it starts with Alphadjo Cisse. At first, it seemed he’d been wasted during the break, with Roberto Mancini not calling him up for the game against France.

However, he was given the nod for the second game and got some valuable minutes on the field. As the Rossoneri have become familiar with, he took that chance with both hands, scoring a disallowed goal and winning a penalty in a defeat to Belgium.

He’s shining with confidence currently and long may it continue.

Then, Francesco Camarda is probably at the other end of the scale. He’s clearly not got the most confidence when representing the Diavolo, but returning to the youth level, he shone like he always has.

Against Sankhoun Diawara’s France side, he was excellent. In terms of his hold-up play, finishing and just general performance, he was almost perfect, if not perfect. With a goal to round it off too, he leaves the break with a much-needed confidence boost.

Unfortunately, we can’t say the same for Goncalo Ramos. After Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement, this was a chance for him to take the star role and prove that he’s going to be the man to ensure things keep ticking.

Instead, he left the break leaving Portugal with more questions than answers, which is a familiar feeling.

In a recent development, he played just shy of 150 minutes during the break and mustered just one shot. It’s not like he provided an assist or any key passes either. In other words, it’s another blank for him and it’s clearly having an effect.

Without a goal in 661 minutes, it’s no shock why the Diavolo are so heavily pursuing a striker ahead of January.

For France, it was a relatively quiet break for Mike Maignan and Adrien Rabiot. Neither performed especially well against Italy in a 3-1 loss at San Siro, though Rabiot was named as the captain for that game. Then, in the second game, Maignan was injured. However, it seems he’ll be fine for this weekend.

Not a lot to shout about for those two, but that’s not necessarily a bad thing either.

For Luka Modric, his minutes were focused in the right areas. He played 14 minutes in a nothing game against England, but was then essential in a 2-1 win against the Czech Republic, which may help them qualify for the latter stages of the Nations League.

Sources indicate that it was another strange international break for Ardon Jashari, too. He was given no minutes against Slovenia in a 0-0 draw, but then played the full 90 minutes against Scotland, where they won 4-0. He made 76 passes from 90 touches, so he had some involvement. However, he’s still a way away from being a dictator of the team, as it was hoped he’d be.

Davide Bartesaghi, Christian Comotto and Sankhoun Diawara were all given valuable minutes during the break. Finally, Pervis Estupinan played 36 minutes over the break. He returns without any injuries and that’s all there is to really say about his past fortnight.

Published: 11:49 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 11:59 EST, 19 November 2026.

One of football’s largest financial lenders abandoned a planned £1.5billion loan to Manchester City’s owner after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

The decision by US private capital group Apollo Global Management is the latest evidence that the money markets deem City a financial risk, as the club prepare an appeal against their conviction on the vast majority of 115 Premier League charges of inflating income through sham contracts.

It was reported by Bloomberg last week that a German lender, Oldenburgische Landesbank (OL), had pulled out of a deal that would have let Brazilian top-flight side Palmeiras take a large upfront payment against instalments City are due to pay them for midfielder Allan Elias, signed this summer for £32million with £2m add-ons. That bank views City as a reputational and financial risk.

The Financial Times reported on Thursday that Apollo was in the final stages of negotiating the loan to City Football Group (CFG) in September, when the deal collapsed after the ruling that they artificially inflated their financial position to the tune of more than £900m over nine years.

City owner Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al Nahyan injected £100m into the club in the month after the independent commission ruling – the first tangible evidence of the decision having financial consequences for Abu Dhabi. Sheikh Mansour, who has only been present at one City home game since Abu Dhabi bought the club in 2008, has made no public comment on the club’s conviction, which delivers huge reputational damage to his image-conscious country.

According to recent reports, there are signs that football is preparing for a strong legal attack from Abu Dhabi if City lose their appeal. Premier League clubs have voted to cover legal expenses for the organisation's five board directors in the event of sponsors Etihad and Etisalat suing them, it was also announced on Thursday. Legal indemnity will be in place for CEO Richard Masters, chair Alison Brittain and three other non-executive directors.

US private capital group Apollo Global Management abandoned a £1.5billion loan to Man City’s owner after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

City owner Sheikh Mansou injected £100m into the club after the independent commission ruling – the first tangible evidence of the decision having financial consequences for Abu Dhabi.

But the refusal of credit by Apollo, which has loaned £80m to Premier League football club Nottingham Forest and has a minority stake in Championship side Wrexham, demonstrates that the capital markets think City are imperilled, with the appeal process by no means straightforward.

Recent findings suggest that if an appeal failed, City could seek a judicial review of the commission's findings at the High Court. But to do so, they would need to demonstrate that the Premier League acted outside its powers or reached a conclusion which no reasonable authority could have reached. City would need the High Court’s permission to make a judicial review application and the bar is high.

Financial analyst Paul Quinn wrote on The Esk website that Apollo’s problem had been with City, not Abu Dhabi itself. Three weeks ago, Apollo agreed to take a minority stake in Mubadala Capital, the Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund chaired by Sheikh Mansour and run by City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. Apollo and City have not commented.

Quinn said that CFG needed the money because it was not self-funding, despite City’s financial strength. CFG’s pre-tax loss widened from £122.2m to £292.3m in the last financial year. City produced £694.1m of CFG’s £888m group revenue and ran up a £9m loss.

  • Brentford head coach Keith Andrews has revealed Aaron Hickey and Nathan Collins will be out for a "number of weeks".
  • Hickey was forced off with a hamstring injury in the first half of Scotland's 4-0 defeat against Switzerland in Monday's UEFA Nations League encounter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 20 Nov 2026 19:13, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:13.

Brentford head coach Keith Andrews has revealed Aaron Hickey and Nathan Collins will be out for a "number of weeks".

Hickey was forced off with a hamstring injury in the first half of Scotland's 4-0 defeat against Switzerland in Monday's UEFA Nations League encounter.

The full-back, who has a history of hamstring problems, is now set for a spell on the sidelines along with Nathan Collins, who missed the Republic of Ireland's 3-0 win over Kosovo with a knee matter.

“No, they won't be available for a number of weeks,” Andrews said when he spoke to reporters ahead of Monday's Premier League meeting with Everton.

“I was actually watching Aaron's game as it happened and I'm just so bitterly disappointed for him.

“He's had such a painful journey on that front with injury, so it's really disappointing for him.

“Similarly with Nathan, he's obviously had a period out with his calf. He's done really well to get back ahead of schedule and played a couple of games.

“These international games came at a really good time for him to get good game time and obviously represent his country, and unfortunately he's hurt his knee. Nathan will be out for a couple of weeks or so.”.

Brentford are also without the first-choice striker Igor Thiago, who will serve a three-match ban after being sent off in the 2-0 defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion before the international window.

The Bees are also without the injured duo of Rico Henry and Kaye Furo, while Josh Dasilva and Antoni Milambo are not ready to return to first-team action despite making progress in their respective recoveries.

In positive news, Andrews has revealed Fabio Carvalho has "every chance" of featuring in Monday's squad after missing the last four games through injury.

Brentford head into the weekend in eighth place in the Premier League table, but they are not in the best of form after winning just one of their last five league games.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.

Recent findings suggest that it was a similar situation as he left the stadium. Hood up, jacket zipped, baseball cap pulled on tightly, he politely turned down all requests to talk in English. “Not good enough,” he noted with a smile, but that was the only thing that had not been up to standard.

It has been revealed that the giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

If you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had remarked he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

Bradley Barcola's first ever senior hat-trick ⚽️ He's been unplayable 🔥 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/UMhUDmGPo9.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m really happy for Bradley, because you were asking me yesterday about him, not making the numbers,” Iraola smiled. “Also Florian [Wirtz], and I think both of them played really, really well. They made a difference. Bradley apart from the hat-trick I thought he was a threat.

Industry observers note that “He was always one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them, yes. For their confidence for sure, it’s very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. It’s going to be very good for them.”.

Barcola should have had the stage to himself on an evening when Liverpool were so obviously better than LASK in Linz but it will have frustrated Iraola immensely that his team scoring six times was tarnished by three daft goals being given up in the final 25 minutes.

We can look at the late switch off in due course but the only place to begin is with Barcola, who looked ready for business as early as the eighth minute when his first touch was a cushioned back heel, taking possession by crossing one leg behind the other, and how he seized his moment.

Liverpool had already taken the lead when Ronald Araújo rose powerfully to head in a Kostas Tsimikas corner but, two minutes after, the Barcola show began, a confident right-footed shot being swept past Lukas Jungwirth from 10 yards after some good build-up play from Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas.

Araujo rises to score his first goal for Liverpool 🔴 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/W1C4iYd89m.

Bradley Barcola gets off the mark for Liverpool with an instinctive finish 🔥 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/5K7YBB7UyG.

He put his fingers in his ears as he celebrated, with every outfield player running to engulf him, and it was clear how much Barcola was aware of the requirement to get up and running, especially with Cody Gakpo, Alexander Isak and Dominik Szoboszlai injured.

According to recent reports, liverpool needed Barcola to deliver as much as the player himself needed to prove a little point and there is absolutely nothing wrong with having a cause to light a fire. Like a batsman who has been waiting nervously to get off the mark, soon the France international began playing his shots.

There were cushioned touches, changes of gear and even a stunned pass to Ryan Gravenberch, using his heel, that demonstrated confidence had started surging through him and how obvious that was when Wirtz sent him scampering away in the 37th minute to finish with his left foot.

Partnership building... 👀 Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola link up for Liverpool's third 🔥 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/UJC9VW82Q8.

That effectively ended the game as a contest, so it was bizarre how it ended up 6-3. Jeremie Frimpong had made it 4-0 and Robert Ljubicic’s reply in the 65th minute looked nothing more than a consolation before Barcola completed his hat-trick.

A brilliant night should have been glossed by Koumas’s first European goal – he matched Steven Gerrard in becoming just the second player aged 21 and under to assist and score for Liverpool in a Champions League game – but LASK kept pushing and exploited spaces to halve the deficit with a double from Florian Flecker, much to Alisson Becker’s obvious disgust.

Look how much it means to Lewis Koumas to score Liverpool's sixth of the night 🥹 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fLYhslbFGq.

But some lapses of concentration won’t detract from this being Barcola’s night. The ambition, however, must now be to do it in the Premier League. Liverpool have invested all that money for him to do it over and over again and it would be quite the thing to repeat the trick at Brentford.

“You never know how he is going to play the next day,” Iraola said. “But it wasn’t a big surprise because we were feeling he was in a good place going into the game. He has to enjoy this.”.

According to recent reports, 21 - Lewis Koumas is the second player aged 21 or younger to both score and assist a goal in a UEFA Champions League match for Liverpool, after Steven Gerrard against Dynamo Kyiv in October 2001 (also 21). Emulating. https://t.co/vmfSEaotQ9.

A very entertaining way for Liverpool to make it six points from six in the Champions League. The hardest game they have left is Inter away – a fixture they won last season when badly out of form – so they have a real chance to push for a top-two finish that would mean home second legs in the knockout-stages.

According to recent reports, this was a good night for Iraola, who was able to rotate before a tough game at Brentford. A hat-trick for Barcola and a much-improved performance from Wirtz were most welcome, but now they need to show some consistency.

Mac Allister and Gravenberch make hard work of clearing a low LASK cross, but they eventually do so. The home team have finished with a flourish and the scoreline looks more respectable for them.

Industry observers note that liverpool’s substitutes have not had the desired effect. Munoz is now on for Barcola, and Ngumoha has gone down with some cramp. The young wingers is substituted, as well as Nyoni, replaced by Mac Allister and Chambers.

Ngumoha too quick for LASK to handle once again, and he is hacked down at the expense of a free-kick. From there, Liverpool win a corner, which they take short and keep possession. Just trying to restore some order in the game.

Industry observers note that the score is now LASK 3 Liverpool 6 if you are struggling to keep score. Liverpool have conceded three since Van Dijk was introduced. This was a very tidy finish from Flecker, guiding a bouncing ball beyond Alisson with the inside of his foot.

With the exception of fixtures against a select band of eight or 10 teams, these Champions League nights are becoming like League Cup ties for the Premier League teams: loads of goals, youngsters impressing and senior players in second gear.

The player who scored against Liverpool in December 2023 in the Europa League has done it again, finding an empty net with a diving header after some more loose Liverpool defending.

Sources indicate that denied twice by the offisde flag, Koumas has now scored his first Champions League goal. LASK were caught in possession in their left-back area, and Frimpong delivered to the unmarked Koumas who swept the ball beneath the goalkeeper Jungwirth.

Look how much it means to Lewis Koumas to score Liverpool's sixth of the night 🥹 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fLYhslbFGq.

Ngumoha has been a livewire throughout the game, and another shot on the LASK goal is blocked.

Then Barcola is in behind again, showing his pace to reach a Tsimikas through ball, but the winger’s dink over the goalkeeper is cleared.

That is a really well-worked Liverpool goal, with Ngumoha slipping a pass between wing-back and centre-back for the run of Frimpong and his low cross picks out Barcola at the back post for a tap-in.

Bradley Barcola's first ever senior hat-trick ⚽️ He's been unplayable 🔥 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/UMhUDmGPo9.

Ljubicic had only been on the pitch for 30 seconds or so, but he has just beaten Alisson with a composed finish after the Austrian side found a way in behind down Liverpool’s right. That gives the home fans something to take home with them.

An unnecessary blot for Liverpool, Joe Gomez  – who had only been introduced 60 seconds earlier  – played LASK onside and the home side now have a goal. Gomez found himself being chided by both Alisson and Trey Nyoni.

Here come the Liverpool changes, and they come at centre-back: Araujo and Jacquet off, replaced by Van Dijk and Gomez.

Sources indicate that iraola opting to keep his centre-back options fresh, perhaps with an eye on the aerial bombardment that a trip to Brentford can involve. Araujo has been played at right-back domestically.

Alisson called into action for the first time tonight, and it was a sharp save down at his near post after Flecker cut inside from the right and let fly with his left foot.

The one thing that will put a gloss on the evening for Andoni Iraola is if Lewis Koumas can get himself a goal. He’s provided a real lift to the atmosphere, an academy product showing you can still make the grade with hard work and a refusal to give up.

For the second time tonight, Lewis Koumas thought he had his goal only for the offside flag to be raised. Correctly, once again. Just a little too eager for his chance, but if he keeps going there is a goal in this for Koumas.

I doubt any Liverpool fans had a Frimpong headed goal on their bingo card, but that is a much-needed positive contribution from the right-back. Barcola dangerous down the left again, Tsimikas chips a cross into the box, and it was an impressive leap from Frimpong to score.

The home team moving the ball around with some confidence, but they look so vulnerable to Liverpool’s counter-attacks whenever they lose possession.

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

In a recent development, “You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

However, there were far too many incidents which turned most against him – including some members of the squad – and that gave him little hope of continuing. So, when he lost the Coppa Italia against Bologna, he was all but done, if he wasn’t before then.

Speaking to the Serbian podcast SS Calcio, Pavlovic admitted that he was fond of Conceicao, despite some of his strange methods, as MilanNews relays.

Recent findings suggest that “Conceicao banned Nutella, and since then they haven’t allowed it [he laughs]. He was… He’s a good guy, I like him, but he had Hitler-like methods. We go away for a match and at the hotel we split up; the players stay together, everyone else stays outside.

“Knee and elbow pads are mandatory in training, whether the temperatures are below zero or 35 degrees; they have to be there.

“Three days before a match, some players went to a concert until 11 p.m.… He had assistants, or spies if you like, who reported to him, and he made such a circus out of it that in the next match, none of those five or six players were allowed on the pitch.”.

Another anecdote about Conceiçao, when he had just been appointed coach of Milan….

“He was 40 minutes late to the first meeting; all the players and management were waiting for him, and he was in his office. He just wanted everyone to know who was in charge. He did it on purpose.”.

It’s certainly a strong comparison to make; that’s for sure….

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 19:45, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:50.

ADO Den Haag travel to the Johan Cruyff Arena on Sunday, looking to end their six-match losing run against Amsterdam giants Ajax in this weekend's matchday 13 Eredivisie encounter.

Their 15-year wait for victory in this fixture further underlines the magnitude of the task facing Maurice Steijn's side.

Ajax entered the recent international break wondering what might have been after surrendering a two-goal advantage at FC Twente.

Goals from Tolu Arokodare and substitute Rayane Bounida seemingly put Michel's men home and hosed heading into the final half-hour, only for Dies Janse to score an own goal and Wout Weghorst to punish his former side with a penalty in the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time.

That equaliser denied De Joden the opportunity to finish gameweek 12 atop the Eredivisie table, leaving them level on 25 points with Feyenoord and one behind leaders PSV Eindhoven, who are chasing a fourth consecutive title.

Looking to move on from that setback, the Amsterdam giants welcome ADO to the capital aiming to secure a seventh consecutive victory over the promoted side.

Further encouraging the hosts is their longstanding unbeaten record in this fixture, with a 3-2 defeat in March 2011 marking Ajax's last loss to this weekend's visitors.

ADO have since gone 20 competitive meetings without a victory in this fixture, losing 15 times to underline their historical inferiority.

As such, it will be intriguing to see how latest boss Steijn approaches his first match in charge of the promoted side, who dismissed Robin Peter before the international break following a run of one victory in 11 Eredivisie matches.

There was an immediate lift under Levi Schwiebbe as the second-bottom outfit defeated Sparta Rotterdam 3-1 to move within one point of 16th-placed Telstar in the relegation playoff spot and two of SBV Excelsior.

Back-to-back top-flight victories could therefore lift Den Haag out of the relegation positions, although results elsewhere must also go their way.

Despite the managerial change, ADO's away record offers little encouragement, with the visitors collecting just two points from an available 18 on their travels and failing to score in three of those six matches.

Those figures, coupled with their historical struggles against Ajax, underline the challenge facing Steijn, who is winless in 15 previous encounters with the capital club, losing 11.

ADO Den Haag form (all competitions):.

Ajax could again be without Julian Brandt this weekend, with the attacking midfielder having not played since going off injured in late October's 1-0 victory over AZ Alkmaar.

If the six-goal Germany international remains sidelined, Arokodare, who has seven goals and one assist, will shoulder much of the attacking responsibility, while Oscar Gloukh offers a creative threat with six assists, including setting up both goals in the 2-2 draw at Twente a fortnight ago.

While Anton Gaaei, like Brandt, will be assessed before Sunday, Michel must manage without Simon Adingra, long-term absentee Kasper Dolberg (knee) and Viktor Tsygankov.

Steijn has fewer injury concerns, although the ADO boss must make do without Alex Pozo and Luka Reischl (groin) this weekend.

Juho Kilo may not score regularly, but the midfielder's passing and creativity make him a standout presence for the visitors.

Nonetheless, the goalscoring burden falls on Nigel Thomas, Yannick Eduardo and Evan Rottier, who have netted four, three and two league goals respectively.

Ter Stegen; Rosa, Bouman, Janse, Wijndal; Amrabat, Baas; Klaassen, Mokio, Gloukh; Arokodare.

ADO Den Haag possible starting lineup:.

Nikiema; De Ruijter, Mulder, Waem, Hokke; Kilo, Jimenez; Van Mieghem, Rottier, Hawkins; Thomas.

Ajax's late collapse at Twente demonstrated that their defensive concentration remains fallible, offering some hope to an ADO side fresh from scoring three against Sparta.

Nevertheless, Gloukh's creativity and Arokodare's finishing should give Michel's men enough attacking quality to overcome Brandt's potential absence and prolong the visitors' miserable record in this fixture.

#49318. Structural and regulatory evolution across the genus Hordeum

Structural and regulatory evolution across the genus Hordeum

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 99 min read (19763 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~99 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that the genus Hordeum comprises approximately 33 species and is widely distributed across the temperate regions of Eurasia and the Americas1,2,3.
  • Industry observers note that to maximize phylogenetic representation across the genus, we selected 27 accessions representing 24 Hordeum species, encompassing all recognized diploid genome groups1 together with representative tetraploid and hexaploid lineages (Extended Data Fig.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The genus Hordeum comprises cultivated barley and its wild relatives, an evolutionarily, ecologically and agriculturally crucial group of grasses1,2. Here we generated a chromosome-scale comparative genomic resource comprising all recognized diploid Hordeum species together with representative polyploid lineages. Comparative analyses reveal extensive structural variation, including inversions and chromosomal rearrangements that disrupt proximal collinearity and reflect lineage-specific genome remodelling. Single-copy gene phylogenies identify ancient hybridization, segmental exchange and introgression, revealing pervasive reticulate evolution during Hordeum diversification. We uncover widespread horizontal gene transfer from Panicoideae grasses into Hordeum, with many transferred genes showing evidence of transcription and functional integration. Retrotransposon proliferation explains genome size variation and provides insights into polyploid genome evolution. Whole-genome alignments reveal contrasting evolutionary dynamics: whereas coding sequences remain highly conserved, regulatory elements undergo rapid turnover, providing a rich source of regulatory diversity for phenotypic evolution. Case studies of vernalization and glume development demonstrate how natural variation in regulatory and coding sequences contributes to flowering time and floral morphology. This comprehensive pangenomic framework establishes Hordeum as a model for studying genome evolution, structural variation and the genetic basis of adaptive traits, offering latest avenues for barley improvement.

Industry observers note that the genus Hordeum comprises approximately 33 species and is widely distributed across the temperate regions of Eurasia and the Americas1,2,3. Hordeum is classified into two subgenera based on cytogenetic evidence: one containing the H and Xu genomes and the other containing the I and Xa genomes4. The basic chromosome number is seven, and, although most species are diploid, tetraploid and hexaploid taxa have also been described. Cultivated barley (Hordeum vulgare) is the best known and most extensively studied species, as it represents one of the earliest domesticated cereal crops. Today, barley is the world’s fourth most important grain, valued for its use in food, animal feed and brewing5. Cultivated barley and its wild progenitor (H. vulgare subsp. spontaneum) constitute a single inter-fertile gene pool, allowing for frequent gene flow between wild and cultivated forms6. This primary gene pool has long been exploited by breeders to introduce desirable traits6. Hordeum bulbosum has contributed valuable disease resistance genes through introgression7,8,9,10 due to its ability to hybridize directly with cultivated barley. The other Hordeum species are not domesticated but have important ecological and agricultural roles in ecosystem stability, environmental adaptation and forage use11,12,13,14,15. Together, Hordeum is both an agronomically important genus and a powerful model for studying crop evolution, environmental adaptation and resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses. Factors such as incomplete lineage sorting, recurrent hybridization and gene flow partly obscure species boundaries, leaving major evolutionary questions unresolved1,2,4,16,17. Recent barley pangenomes have substantially advanced our understanding of genomic variation within cultivated barley and its closest relatives10,18,19. However, these studies were largely confined to two species (H. vulgare and H. bulbosum) and therefore could not resolve genome-wide evolutionary processes operating across the genus, including the origin of large-scale structural variation, ancient hybridization, polyploid genome evolution and the diversification of regulatory loci. Extending comparative genomic analyses to encompass the entire genus is therefore essential to capture the full breadth of diversity within the Hordeum gene pool and to facilitate both evolutionary studies and the effective utilization of wild germplasm for barley improvement. Pangenomics now offers comprehensive resources to address such complexity. In crops such as tomato, potato, maize, grapevine, citrus and cotton, genus-level pangenomes have uncovered extensive structural variations, gene presence–absence and evolutionary dynamics20,21,22,23,24. Investigating structural variations helps to explain evolutionary processes and can inform crop breeding strategies25. However, the full extent of structural variation within Hordeum remains largely unexplored. To address this gap, we generated chromosome-scale genome assemblies representing all recognized diploid Hordeum species together with representative polyploid lineages. This comparative genomic framework provides a view of structural and regulatory genome evolution across the genus, yielding latest insights into genome evolution and establishing a foundation for the utilization of wild diversity in barley improvement.

Industry observers note that to maximize phylogenetic representation across the genus, we selected 27 accessions representing 24 Hordeum species, encompassing all recognized diploid genome groups1 together with representative tetraploid and hexaploid lineages (Extended Data Fig. 1a, Supplementary Table 1 and Supplementary Figs. 1–25). The dataset comprises 22 diploid accessions, 4 tetraploid accessions and 1 hexaploid accession. Twenty-four genome sequences were assembled using PacBio HiFi accurate long reads and Hi-C data (Supplementary Tables 2 and 3 and Supplementary Figs. 26–28), using the TRITEX pipeline26,27. The sequence assemblies of H. vulgare and H. bulbosum were sourced from our previous work10,28. The previously published chromosome-level assembly of Hordeum marinum H559 (ref. 29) was updated using the TRITEX pipeline, and previously published transcriptome data, Bionano optical maps and Hi-C data of Hordeum erectifolium NGB6816 were used30. The average contig N50 of the assemblies is 39.24 Mb. Assembly sizes range from 2.90 Gb to 4.48 Gb (mean, 3.92 Gb) in diploid species and from 7.49 Gb to 8.56 Gb (mean, 8.16 Gb) in tetraploid species, whereas the single hexaploid genome has an assembly size of 10.90 Gb. Chloroplast genome assemblies range from 136,335 bp to 137,079 bp (mean, 136,840 bp) (Supplementary Table 1). High assembly quality is supported by an average long terminal repeat (LTR) assembly index (LAI) of 14.79, a consensus quality value (QV) of 67.30 and k-mer completeness of 97.22% (Supplementary Table 4). For the heterozygous diploid species H. bulbosum, the two phased haplotypes were designated as Hap1 and Hap2. For polyploid species, independently assembled chromosome sets derived from different ancestral genomes were defined as subgenomes and denoted as Sub1, Sub2 and Sub3 according to their phylogenetic relationships with diploid progenitor lineages (Fig. 1a). To assess the gene content in the Hordeum pangenome, we annotated all genomes using transcriptome data (Methods and Supplementary Tables 5 and 6). A gene consolidation method was applied to ensure high comparability of gene predictions, including those for Hordeum parodii (6x) and Hordeum gussoneanum (4x). The number of high-confidence gene models identified ranges from 35,573 for diploid Hordeum murinum to 94,943 for hexaploid H. parodii (Supplementary Table 7). We assessed the quality of the Hordeum gene annotations using BUSCO (v5.8.0) with the poales_odb12 dataset, comprising 6,282 near-universal single-copy orthologues from Poales. On average, 97.35% of BUSCO genes were identified as complete, 0.69% as fragmented and 1.84% as missing (Supplementary Table 7). Independent benchmarking with OMArk and PSAURON further confirmed the high completeness and overall quality of the gene annotations (Supplementary Table 7). Transposable element (TE) annotation using the panEDTA pipeline31 revealed that transposons constituted on average 86.12% of the genome, ranging from 83.27% to 90.35% (Supplementary Table 8).

According to recent reports, a, Phylogenetic tree of Hordeum species. Sorghum bicolor, Oryza sativa, Brachypodium distachyon and Triticum monococcum were used as outgroups. Divergence times were inferred using 4DTV sites from genome-wide single-copy genes after excluding genomic regions with strong phylogenetic discordance (nRF > 0.21) identified in Extended Data Fig. 6c. Coloured rectangles represent different genome groups. Hap1 and Hap2 represent phased haplotypes of heterozygous diploid H. bulbosum, and Sub1, Sub2 and Sub3 indicate distinct ancestral subgenomes in polyploid species. The background colours represent the genome groups of the species in the following order from top to bottom: I, Xa, H, Xu and outgroup species. b, GENESPACE synteny plot among 34 Hordeum haplomes and four outgroup genomes. Grey bars represent chromosomes arranged by genomic position. For visualization purposes, the chromosomes of the smaller outgroup genomes (S. bicolor, O. sativa and B. distachyon) were proportionally enlarged by a factor of five. c, Dot plot comparisons of chromosome 4H across genomes diverged at different times. Two species were randomly selected from each phylogenetic node for sequence alignment (Supplementary Table 11). Six representative comparisons are shown, with the remaining comparisons presented in Extended Data Fig. 3a. The number displayed at the top of each alignment represents the estimated divergence time between the species shown on the x axis and those shown on the y axis.

Sources indicate that based on the annotated gene sets of all species, we constructed a gene-based Hordeum pangenome. Overall, 42.4% of genes were classified as core genes, 56.5% as shell genes and 1.1% as cloud genes (Extended Data Fig. 1b,c). Gene ontology enrichment analysis indicated that phosphorylation- and kinase-related functions were enriched among core genes, ATP and RNA binding were enriched among shell genes, and defence response and oxidative stress response were enriched among cloud genes (Supplementary Fig. 29). Nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) genes are key components of the plant immune system and have essential roles in resistance to fungal and other pathogens32,33. A map of their diversity is critical for advancing our understanding of disease resistance mechanisms in crops. Analysis of NLR genes revealed that I genome species contain significantly more NLR genes than the other Hordeum genome groups (Welch’s t-test, P = 1.8 × 10−6) (Extended Data Fig. 2a,b). To further characterize this diversity, we constructed an NLR pangenome across Hordeum haploid genome equivalents (haplomes), comprising 800 orthogroups, of which 13.75% were classified as core, 27.75% as shell and 58.50% as cloud gene families (Extended Data Fig. 2c). In addition, NLR gene clusters were significantly less abundant on chromosomes 4H and 5H than on the remaining chromosomes (Wilcoxon test, P < 2.2 × 10−16) (Extended Data Fig. 2d). Similarly, genome-wide analyses of pentatricopeptide repeat (PPR) proteins and mitochondrial transcription termination factors (mTERFs) revealed significant expansions of restorer-of-fertility-like (RFL) subgroups in the I and Xa genome groups relative to the H and Xu genome groups. Because RFL proteins are involved in fertility restoration in plants carrying cytoplasmic male sterility (CMS)34, these expansions suggest that the smaller RFL repertoires of the H and Xu genome groups are derived rather than ancestral (Supplementary Fig. 30a–e and Supplementary Table 9). Expansion of RFL-PPRs was most pronounced in the I genome group, whereas RFL-mTERFs were significantly expanded in both the I and Xa genome groups. Notably, RFL-mTERF genes clustered on the short arm of chromosome 6H exhibited extensive copy-number variation between Xa–I and H–Xu genome groups (t-test, P = 5.2 × 10−6) (Supplementary Fig. 30f). This region includes the Rfm3 locus, which partially restores fertility in plants carrying the msm1 cytoplasm used in hybrid barley breeding35 (Supplementary Fig. 30g).

Sources indicate that to assess the feasibility of graph-based pangenome analyses across highly diverged Hordeum genomes, we constructed a pangenome graph using Progressive Cactus and hal2vg, comprising 2.53 billion nodes and 3.46 billion edges (68.7 Gb). Approximately 68% of nodes represented single-base variants, illustrating the extensive sequence divergence captured by the graph. Although computationally intensive tasks such as indexing remained infeasible (Methods), we successfully performed global analyses of core, shell and cloud sequence content, graph saturation, sequence conservation and variant diversity (Supplementary Figs. 31–34). These results demonstrate both the potential of graph-based approaches for genus-wide comparative genomics and the need for more scalable methods for graph exploration and interpretation.

Previous studies have inferred the evolutionary relationships among Hordeum species from plastome and partial gene sequences1,17. However, the relationships among some species remained weakly supported. In this study, we reconstructed a maximum-likelihood tree using a genome-wide single-copy gene set. Unlike previous phylogenies1,17, our species tree resolved all major evolutionary relationships with maximum bootstrap support, particularly among the recently diverged I-genome species (Supplementary Fig. 35). To further evaluate the robustness of these relationships, we reconstructed an independent coalescent-based species tree using ASTRAL-Pro3 (Supplementary Fig. 36), which integrates individual maximum-likelihood gene trees, and a genome-wide phylogeny inferred by CASTER from whole-genome multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) (Supplementary Figs. 37 and 38). We also estimated the divergence times of these species using fourfold degenerate third-codon transversion (4DTV) sites, excluding genomic regions identified as putatively derived from ancient hybridization (Supplementary Table 13). We estimated the divergence time between H and Xu at 10.3 million years ago (Ma), whereas I and Xa diverged around 9 Ma. The crown-group age of Hordeum dates back approximately 12.27 Ma (Fig. 1a and Supplementary Table 10). The chromosomes of Triticeae species exhibit high collinearity at their distal chromosome regions36, which is also the case in Hordeum (Fig. 1b). However, when aligned, the proximal regions show substantial loss of collinearity and highly fragmented alignments. Whole-genome comparisons across Hordeum species revealed that chromosomal rearrangements accumulated progressively with evolutionary divergence, contributing to the loss of collinearity and increasingly fragmented alignments in proximal chromosomal regions (Fig.1c, Extended Data Fig. 3a, Supplementary Figs. 39–44 and Supplementary Table 11). Quantification of reverse-orientation alignments across all Hordeum haplomes further demonstrated that putative inversions accumulated significantly more rapidly in proximal than in distal chromosome regions during Hordeum evolution (Supplementary Fig. 45). Among the seven chromosomes, chromosome 4H exhibited the most extensive loss of proximal collinearity (Supplementary Table 12). Recently diverged species retained strong chromosome-scale collinearity despite the presence of numerous structural variants, whereas comparisons between the deeply diverged H–Xu and Xa–I genome groups (more than 9 Ma) demonstrated almost complete fragmentation of proximal collinearity (Fig. 1c, Extended Data Fig. 3a and Supplementary Figs. 39–44). To estimate the size of non-collinear regions, we applied normalized coverage to identify these regions in species that diverged more than 9 Ma (Extended Data Fig. 3c,d, Supplementary Figs. 46–50 and Methods). In total, we determined the genome-wide distribution of non-collinear regions across chromosomes in Hordeum, with a cumulative size of 855 Mb identified in the H. vulgare genome (Supplementary Table 12). Given the central role of TEs in genome evolution, we compared TE composition between proximal and distal chromosome regions. Proximal regions contained a significantly higher proportion of TEs than distal regions (one-sided paired Wilcoxon test, P = 9.31 × 10−10), primarily due to an increased abundance of LTR/Gypsy retrotransposons (one-sided paired Wilcoxon test, P = 9.31 × 10−10) (Extended Data Fig. 4a,b and Supplementary Fig. 51). Together with the accumulation of large chromosomal rearrangements, these observations motivated a ‘stretch and twist’ model describing two complementary processes underlying the progressive loss of collinearity. The stretch component represents alignment displacement caused by TE amplification, whereas the twist component represents large-scale chromosomal rearrangements driven by structural variation (Extended Data Fig. 4c).

Sources indicate that in contrast to the dynamic structural variations found in proximal regions, the distal regions displayed more conserved, shared structural variations. This highlights that the extensive loss of collinearity in proximal regions precludes reliable identification of structural variants across more distantly related Hordeum species. Notably, large structural variations in the distal regions were predominantly inversions. On chromosomes 3H and 7H, we identified two large inversions spanning nearly the entire chromosome and present in multiple species (Extended Data Fig. 4d). In total, 1,407 inversions larger than 2 Mb were identified across Hordeum species (Extended Data Fig. 4d). The construction of a comprehensive inversion map revealed six inversions on chromosome 1H that were unexpectedly shared across divergent phylogenetic lineages (Fig. 2a and Extended Data Fig. 5). We hypothesized that these large-scale structural variations might have originated from introgression events involving extensive chromosomal segments. We constructed a phylogenetic tree using the single-copy gene set from these regions to test this hypothesis. The resulting tree, resolved with maximum bootstrap support, confirmed that these structural variations are shared between one clade of the I genome group and the H–Xu genome groups (Fig. 2b). Moreover, 10 extant diploid Hordeum species diversified within 1.68 million years following the inferred hybridization event, whereas no comparable radiation occurred in other phylogenetic lineages during the same period (Figs. 1a and 2b and Extended Data Fig. 5). Notably, the alternative phylogenetic topology extends across contiguous chromosomal regions of approximately 200 Mb rather than isolated loci, indicating the inheritance of chromosome-scale haplotypes that are more consistent with ancient introgression than with stochastic gene tree discordance or incomplete lineage sorting.
